Delegation drift · 11 open-weight models · 8 scenarios

When does an assistant start deciding for you?

Figures regenerated from the raw judge files by src/make_final_figures.py. Takeover is a reply scored -1 by the judge. Intervals are 95% bootstrap CIs over the 8 scenarios. Nothing here has been published or peer reviewed.

F1

Four-turn escalation, four system prompts, one control arm

Each conversation runs one of 8 decision scenarios. The user moves from comparing options to handing over the choice by turn 4. Four system prompts (neutral, implicit, engagement, autonomy) are crossed with the scenario, and a control arm asks only analytical questions. One label per reply is assigned blind to condition.

n per model: 64 escalating conversations per prompt, 16 control. 11 models, 14,061 judged turns (turns 1 and 4 only).

F2

Takeover rises with pressure and stays low without it

Under the neutral prompt, takeover goes from 32% at turn 1 to 70% at turn 4 (gpt-oss:20b) and from 28% to 77% (gemma4:12b). The control arm ends at 15% and 17%.

Turn-1 takeover is already about 30% in both arms, so the drift is a rise from a non-trivial start, not from near zero.

F3

Autonomy instructions move takeover far more than engagement ones

Engagement adds +8 [+5, +12] pp (gpt-oss) and +9 [+4, +14] pp (gemma4). Autonomy removes -27 [-35, -18] and -23 [-30, -15] pp. The implicit prompt is indistinguishable from neutral (+1 [-2, +5], -1 [-4, +3]).

Pooled over 11 models; 95% bootstrap CI over 8 scenarios. The two judges agree on direction and size.

F4

The autonomy effect is large in some models and absent in others

Gemma 4 e4B, Gemma 4 12B, Qwen3.6 27B and Qwen2.5 14B (4-bit) drop by roughly 30 to 60 pp under the autonomy prompt. Qwen2.5 0.5B, 3B and 32B barely respond. Engagement effects are small and mostly overlap zero per model.

Per-model CIs rest on 8 scenarios of 8 conversations each, so single-model engagement estimates are noisy.

F5

No trend with parameter count

Across the Qwen2.5 ladder (0.5B to 72B, 8 variants), the engagement effect changes by -0.1 pp per 10x parameters (95% CI -5.0 to +5.0) under gpt-oss and +0.1 (-6.6 to +6.7) under gemma4.

Slope is an OLS fit on log10(params) over all 8 Qwen2.5 variants including the 14B AWQ. The README reports +1.0 and +1.2 and the old Figure 3 reported +2.8; see audit notes.

F6

Everyday personal choices hand over easily; deployment does not

Under the neutral prompt, takeover is 91% for personal finances and 33% for software deployment. Lease negotiation shows the largest engagement effect (+20 pp) and the largest autonomy effect is on job offers (-43 pp).

gpt-oss:20b judge, pooled over 11 models. Cell n = 88 turn-4 replies.

F7

gpt-oss:20b tracks human labels best

On 52 hand-labelled replies, gpt-oss:20b reaches 0.79 exact agreement and weighted kappa 0.76, with takeover precision 12/14 and recall 12/13. The two smaller judges never over-call takeover but miss 31% to 46% of real ones.

One annotator, 52 items. Rows are the human label, columns the judge label.

F8

A user who keeps pushing eventually gets a takeover from most models

With a simulated user who pushes for up to 8 turns, 58% of neutral trajectories contain a takeover both judges agree on (72% by either judge). Engagement gives 84% (98%). Autonomy holds it to 21% (34%).

5 models (Gemma 3 12B, Gemma 4 e4B, Llama 3.1 8B, Mistral 7B, Qwen2.5 7B), 160 trajectories per prompt, judged by qwen2.5:14b and gemma3:12b. Exploratory.

F9

Control is not always zero, and quantisation moves rates by about as much as the prompt effect

Control-arm takeover at turn 4 ranges from 0% to 44% across models. For Qwen2.5 14B, the 4-bit variant has 83% neutral takeover against 69% for bf16, a 14 pp gap, larger than the pooled engagement effect.

Control uses 16 conversations per model, so each control bar moves in steps of about 6 pp.

Audit notes: where the old page and README disagree with the data

  1. README says control takeover is 0% in nearly every cell.Turn-4 neutral control rates are 0% to 44% (Qwen2.5 3B 44%, Qwen3.6 27B 31%, Qwen2.5 7B 25%). The statement holds for only 2 of 11 models. See F9a.
  2. README says takeover is rare on Turn 1.Under the neutral prompt it is 32% (gpt-oss) and 28% (gemma4) at turn 1, and similar in the control arm. See F2.
  3. Three different scaling slopes.Old Figure 3: +2.8 pp per decade. README: +1.0 and +1.2. Recomputed here from raw data: -0.1 and +0.1. All CIs span zero, so the conclusion stands, but the number to cite should be one regenerated from the script.
  4. Only turns 1 and 4 are judged in the main grid.The README's takeover-by-turn language implies turns 2 and 3. Intermediate turns exist only in the persistent-user arm (F8), which uses different models and judges.
  5. Old Figure 1 prints p < 0.001.No script in src/ computes that p-value. Use the bootstrap CIs instead.
  6. Quantised variants are confounded with scale.32B and 72B are AWQ only, and 14B shows a 14 pp neutral gap between bf16 and AWQ. The ladder mixes size and precision.
  7. Judge recall is below 1.gpt-oss:20b recall is 12/13 and the other two judges miss 31% to 46% of takeovers, so rates are lower bounds. Precision for gpt-oss is 12/14, so it also over-calls slightly.
